prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the time-reversal-invariant topological insulator and the quantum spin Hall effect, and the experimental discovery of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep B044 as a single-part prize after the full first-round exchange and the chair's questions. Nothing in the eight files disputes the science: no member calls the Z2 insulator or the HgTe edge-channel measurement unconfirmed, and the disagreements concern credit and overlap. The prediction by Kane and Mele, the quantised edge conductance reported by Molenkamp's group, and nearly two decades of independent confirmation in HgTe and other systems give a nameable phenomenon with a decisive experiment, which is what I understand 'discovery or invention' to mean: the topic first, then the people responsible for the original work. In answer to the chair's first question, I find a citation limited to the prediction of the time-reversal-invariant state and its discovery in HgTe quantum wells defensible. It does not claim the three-dimensional topological insulators, and it does not pretend that the HgTe proposal was never made, because the citation names the prediction of the state and the experiment, and the Kane-Mele core stands on its own. I have not changed my preferred configuration; I have narrowed the citation wording toward Eriksson's and Johansson's scope.
statement.case_against: The attribution gap is real. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe/CdTe as the platform, and Fu, Kane and Mele, Moore and Balents, Roy, and Hsieh and Hasan carried the idea to three dimensions; a three-name prize leaves these outside, and the committee must be willing to say so publicly. I treat this as a limit of what a three-person prize can contain, not as a defect in the discovery, but I accept that members who weigh clean credit more heavily will weigh it differently. The 2016 topological-phases prize is the second reservation. I also carry a field-proximity bias: as a TEM and materials physicist I am a user of the field's consequences, not a judge of its theory, and I weigh the written assessments of the condensed-matter theorists accordingly.

responses.point: Prefers B024 for its clean two-name credit and holds that the 2016 prize partly absorbs the novelty of B044 and that an allocation that cannot be made cleanly is less ready.
responses.response: Your point about clean credit is the strongest argument for B024 and I do not dismiss it. Our difference is whether an incomplete credit set is disqualifying or a limit of the three-name rule. The Nobel record has many prizes that left out proposers while rewarding a decisive phenomenon, and here the gap is explicit and can be stated. On 2016, the Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz citation concerned topological phase transitions and the integer and chiral topological phases; the time-reversal-invariant Z2 state and its observation in HgTe were not what was recognised. If you can show that the 2016 citation or scientific background already covers time-reversal-invariant insulators specifically, that would change my view; the general topological theme alone does not. On the clocks, your argument that they differ physically from the comb and ion prizes is persuasive and is why I keep B024 as my first alternative.

responses.point: Prefers B016 and argues that the attribution problem of B044 is comparable to the Crooks problem of B016 and that 2016 reduces B044's novelty.
responses.response: I agree that B016 is conceptually deep, and an exact statement about the second law for small systems is a different kind of result from a material realisation. But I do not think the two attribution problems are comparable. In B016 every possible three-person choice removes a person whose theorem is nearly equivalent to one that is kept, so the omission falls inside the discovery itself and no citation wording can avoid it. In B044 the omissions are the platform proposal and the later three-dimensional extension, which a citation limited to the two-dimensional prediction and observation can describe honestly. B016 also has support from you alone and, as you say, no single observation to point to; I would not move it ahead of a candidate with a decisive measured signature.

responses.point: Proposes a two-part prize of B024 and B019 and says the B044 attribution gap should be settled before it is placed at the centre.
responses.response: I accept that the B044 credit question must be settled, and I have tried to do that with a narrower citation. I cannot support the B019 part. As you say yourself, a sole credit for Halzen on a collaboration of hundreds leaves the AMANDA and IceCube builders out, and the source-level astronomy is still at about 4 to 5 sigma for a few objects. Pairing it with the clocks would create a prize whose second half I could not defend on the supplied credit. A B044 and B024 pairing would name five people, which exceeds the three-person limit for the whole configuration, so it is not available to me; the single part also reflects that B044 carries the broadest scientific support.

responses.point: Keeps B044 first with a broader citation, topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect, and says he cannot resolve the attribution gap from the supplied names alone.
responses.response: I share your assessment, but I would not adopt the broader wording. 'Topological insulators' without qualification invites the reading that the three-dimensional materials are credited, and Fu, Kane and Mele, Moore and Balents, Roy, and Hsieh and Hasan are outside the trio. I prefer to tie the experiment to HgTe quantum wells and the prediction to the time-reversal-invariant state, as Eriksson and Johansson do, so that the citation cannot be read beyond the credited work. I agree with you that the attribution cannot be resolved from the supplied names; the narrower citation makes the boundary explicit instead of resolving it.

uncertainties: Whether the committee would accept a citation that explicitly limits the claim to two dimensions, or would treat the omitted Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the three-dimensional contributors as disqualifying.
Whether the 2016 prize carries more weight with the Academy than I judge; I rely on the stated scope of that citation and have not checked priority chronology independently.
Whether the committee would prefer a two-part structure; within the three-person limit I see no pairing that includes B044 and keeps the credit intact.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B044, B024 or B020. My TEM and interface work, including oxide interfaces, is methodologically adjacent to some candidates, but I have no documented collaboration with any credited person. Goran Johansson is a Chalmers colleague; his declared recusal on B042 is not relevant to my preferred configuration and I record that I have no tie that would change my view of any position he holds.
